# Green Party Manifesto 2024 Summary

## Core Vision

The Green Party presents itself as the only party offering genuine hope amid Britain's cost-of-living crisis and climate emergency. They argue that despite being one of the world's richest nations, the UK suffers from crumbling public services, unaffordable housing, and inadequate healthcare—all resulting from deliberate political choices that can be reversed.

## Climate and Energy

The manifesto treats climate action as inseparable from social justice. The party commits to transitioning to zero-carbon far ahead of 2050, with wind providing 70% of electricity by 2030. They would ban new fossil fuel extraction, cancel licences like Rosebank, end fossil fuel subsidies, and introduce a carbon tax starting at £120/tonne. Nuclear power is rejected as expensive and dangerous. Community ownership of renewable energy infrastructure is prioritised, alongside a "just transition" ensuring workers in carbon-intensive industries aren't abandoned.

## Public Services

The NHS would receive £28bn additional annual funding by 2030, with £20bn capital investment. The party opposes privatisation and supports the NHS Reinstatement Bill. Social care would receive £20bn annually, introducing free personal care modelled on Scotland's system. Education funding would increase by £8bn, abolishing tuition fees and restoring maintenance grants.

## Housing

The manifesto promises 150,000 new social homes annually, ending Right to Buy, empowering councils to introduce rent controls, and ending no-fault evictions. A £29bn five-year programme would retrofit homes for energy efficiency.

## Economy and Taxation

The party proposes £40bn average annual green investment, funded through wealth taxes on assets above £10m, aligned capital gains taxation, and a carbon tax potentially raising £80bn by parliament's end. Privatised utilities—railways, water, and major energy retailers—would return to public ownership.

## Workers' Rights

Anti-union legislation since 1979 would be repealed, replaced by a Charter of Workers' Rights. A £15 minimum wage and maximum 10:1 pay ratios would be introduced, alongside movement toward a four-day week.

## Democracy and Rights

The party advocates proportional representation, votes at 16, abolishing the House of Lords, and defending the Human Rights Act. They support Scottish and Welsh self-determination and would scrap hostile environment immigration policies.

## International

The manifesto calls for an immediate Israel-Gaza ceasefire, Palestinian state recognition, ending UK arms exports to Israel, and rejoining the EU. They would sign the UN nuclear weapons prohibition treaty and cancel Trident, while remaining in NATO with reforms.
